html:
The Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi is a fig tree at Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka, said to grow from a cutting of the tree under which the Buddha found enlightenment. Tradition dates its planting to about 288 BCE.

The chronicles say the nun Sanghamitta, daughter of the emperor Ashoka, brought the cutting from Bodh Gaya soon after her brother Mahinda converted the king. It is often called the oldest living tree planted by people with a known date.

The tree tied the island's kings to Theravada Buddhism and made Anuradhapura a pilgrim city, and pilgrims still come in their thousands. In 1985 gunmen blamed on the Tamil Tigers killed well over a hundred people at the site, one of the worst massacres of the civil war.
